items.text:
Posting my notes on the warehouse data migration in case anyone else is prepping for the same move. We're going from the old on-prem SQL cluster to a managed Postgres instance, roughly 140 tables and a bit under two terabytes. The assistant on our team produced a first pass at the table mapping, which was helpful but not something I'd trust blind.

The big surprises so far: three tables have composite keys that the ORM never documented, and a handful of datetime columns are stored as local time without any timezone marker. We also found orphaned rows in the orders table that violate a foreign key nobody enforced. The staging load ran clean but the validation script compared counts only, so it missed truncation in two text fields.

My recommendation is to run row-level checksums, not just counts, and to freeze writes on the source for the cutover window. The vendor's checklist is decent but assumes a much cleaner schema than ours. If anyone has a good approach for reconciling the datetime columns, I'd love to hear it before we schedule the dry run.

intent.requested_action: share approach for reconciling datetime columns
